To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
proteasome inhibitors induce the localisation of NYESO-1 to the centriole in a manner that depends on the C-terminal 150 residues of NYESO1.
the CT antigens NY-ES01 and MAGE-CI can be regulated by post translational processes and that this is mediated via proteosomal degradation.
the cancer/testis (CT) antigens NY-ES0-1 and MACE-C1 are proteasome regulated in tumour cells and are localised to the centrosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of CT antigens and their role in cancer.
understanding the mechanisms governing CT antigen degradation and localisation.
the mechanisms that control the steady state levels and localisation of NYESO-1, MAGE-C1 and other cancer/testis antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the steady-state levels of the cancer/testis (CT) antigens NY-ES0-1 and MACE-C1 are regulated in a cell-type specific manner by the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, and that this process can affect the antigenicity of these antigens.
the CT antigen NY-ESO1 is regulated by proteasome activity, which in turn affects its localisation at the centrosomal region.

the CT antigen NY-ESO1, and MAGE-C2 (MAGE-C1), can be regulated by proteasome-mediated protein degradation, and that this can result in the redistribution of these proteins to centrosomes in the cytoplasm of cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cancer/testis (CT) antigens NY-ES0-1 and MACE-C1 are regulated at the post-translational level by proteasomal mediated degradation.
CT antigens are not only regulated by transcriptional control, but also by post-translional control, which could be a potential target for future therapeutic intervention.
CT antigen stability is regulated at the level of the proteasome, and that this is important for their subcellular localisation and aggregation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT antigens are aggregation-prone and that they can be regulated by proteasome activity in tumour cells.
the steady state level of CT antigens in cancer cells is regulated by proteasome activity.

proteasome inhibitors can increase the levels of NY- ES O-1 and M AGE-C1 in tumour cells, which can potentially lead to an increased antigen presentation of these proteins and therefore an increased immunogenicity in vivo.
